old:
Blood pressure classification per 2017 ACC/AHA guideline (updated 2023):
- Normal: <120/<80 mmHg
- Elevated: 120-129/<80 mmHg
- Stage 1 Hypertension: 130-139/80-89 mmHg
- Stage 2 Hypertension: ≥140/≥90 mmHg
new:
Blood pressure categories (2025 AHA/ACC):
- Normal: systolic <120 AND diastolic <80 mmHg
- Elevated: systolic 120–129 AND diastolic <80 mmHg
- Stage 1: systolic 130–139 OR diastolic 80–89 mmHg
- Stage 2: systolic ≥140 OR diastolic ≥90 mmHg
reason: Correct category logic and unsupported 2023 update label

old:

- Stage 1 HTN + 10-year ASCVD risk <10%: lifestyle modification first, reassess in 3-6 months

new:
- Add medication for average BP ≥140/90, or ≥130/80 with CVD, prior stroke, diabetes, CKD, or PREVENT-CVD 10-year risk ≥7.5%.
- Lower-risk stage 1: initiate medication if average BP remains ≥130/80 after 3–6 months of lifestyle treatment.
- Stage 2: prefer two first-line classes, ideally a single-pill combination, alongside lifestyle treatment.
reason: Replace obsolete risk threshold and add escalation

old: 10-year ASCVD risk calculator: ACC/AHA Pooled Cohort Equations (race/sex-specific)
new: Risk assessment update: use PREVENT-ASCVD in applicable adults aged 30–79. Very-high-risk ASCVD: LDL-C goal <55 mg/dL; other ASCVD generally <70 mg/dL. Treatment intensity and additions depend on risk and response, not one universal ladder.
reason: Update calculator and risk-specific targets

new: Lipid goals: assess ASCVD risk separately; 2026 AHA/ACC recommends LDL-C <55 mg/dL in very-high-risk ASCVD and generally <70 mg/dL in other ASCVD. Do not use a universal LDL <100 target.

new: - Test of cure: recommended about 4 weeks after treatment in pregnancy; in nonpregnant patients, consider when adherence is uncertain, symptoms persist, or reinfection is suspected. Retest at about 3 months for reinfection.

old:
Diagnosis requires ALL 3:
1. Acute onset (rapid onset of signs/symptoms)
2. Middle ear effusion (MEE): bulging tympanic membrane, limited mobility, air-fluid level
3. Middle ear inflammation: distinct erythema OR otalgia interfering with normal activity/sleep
new: Diagnosis: middle-ear effusion must be present, together with moderate/severe TM bulging or new otorrhea not caused by otitis externa; alternatively mild TM bulging with recent (<48 h) otalgia or intense erythema qualifies. Erythema alone is insufficient.
reason: Correct required-vs-alternative diagnostic criteria

old:
DIAGNOSIS CRITERIA (all 3 required):
1. Moderate-to-severe bulging of the tympanic membrane (TM) OR new onset otorrhea not due to external otitis
2. Mild TM bulging + RECENT onset of ear pain (<48h) + intense TM erythema
3. (OR: TM perforation with purulent discharge)
new: DIAGNOSIS: require middle-ear effusion plus moderate/severe TM bulging or new otorrhea not due to otitis externa; OR mild bulging with recent (<48 h) ear pain or intense erythema. These pathways are alternatives, not three simultaneous requirements.
reason: Correct duplicate diagnostic logic

old: Hib #3 (if Hib-OMP)

old:

new:

- Adults 19–49 with eligible risk conditions have a separate risk-based pathway. Prior vaccination changes the schedule; consult the current CDC algorithm.
reason: Update age threshold and include PCV21 without erasing other vaccines

old:
First-line triple therapy (if local clarithromycin resistance <15%):
- Clarithromycin triple: PPI BID + clarithromycin 500mg BID + amoxicillin 1g BID × 14 days
- Bismuth quadruple: PPI BID + bismuth subsalicylate + metronidazole + tetracycline × 10-14 days (preferred if penicillin allergy or high clarithromycin resistance)
new:
Empiric treatment when susceptibility is unknown (ACG 2024):
- Optimized bismuth quadruple therapy for 14 days: PPI twice daily, tetracycline 500 mg orally four times daily, metronidazole 500 mg orally three or four times daily, and bismuth four times daily (product-specific dose).
- Clarithromycin triple therapy is not empiric first-line; use only with demonstrated susceptibility. Rifabutin triple or vonoprazan-amoxicillin dual therapy are alternatives for eligible patients.
reason: Replace obsolete empiric clarithromycin rule while retaining diagnostic and follow-up sections

new: CURRENT SOURCE UPDATE — Eligible disabling stroke: alteplase or tenecteplase within 4.5 hours; selected extended-window cases require imaging criteria. EVT eligibility now includes selected large-core and basilar occlusions. Non-disabling deficits have a different antiplatelet pathway.
reason: Add current scoped recommendation; detailed legacy assertions remain explicitly unresolved

new: CURRENT SOURCE UPDATE — New A–E PE categories guide disposition and advanced therapy. Eligible oral therapy favors DOACs; when parenteral therapy is required, LMWH is generally preferred. Follow symptoms/function for at least one year.
reason: Add current scoped recommendation; detailed legacy assertions remain explicitly unresolved

new: CURRENT SOURCE UPDATE — Shock or probable/definite sepsis: antibiotics immediately, ideally within one hour. Possible sepsis without shock: rapid investigation and antibiotics within three hours if concern persists. Low infection likelihood without shock can justify monitored deferral.
reason: Add current scoped recommendation; detailed legacy assertions remain explicitly unresolved

old: - BP target: <120/80 if tolerated (per SPRINT/evidence); ACEi or ARB for proteinuric CKD (reduces progression)
new: - BP: KDIGO suggests standardized-office systolic BP <120 mmHg when tolerated; this is not a routine-office <120/80 target. ACEi/ARB selection depends on albuminuria and clinical context.
